title: The Arp 240 Galaxy Merger: A Detailed Look at the Molecular Kennicutt─Schmidt Star Formation Law on Subkiloparsec Scales
question: How does the molecular Kennicutt-Schmidt (mK-S) star formation law behave on 500 pc scales across different surface brightness and morphological regimes in the early-stage luminous infrared galaxy merger Arp 240?

data.angular_resolution: native 4'' (~2 kpc) for 7m and 0.6'' (~300 pc) for 12m; re-imaged to 1''
data.sensitivity: 4.7 mJy beam^-1 for NGC 5258 and 6.6 mJy beam^-1 for NGC 5257 per 3 km s^-1 channel

evidence.quote: To transform our measurements of CO ($2\rightarrow1$) to CO ($1\rightarrow0$), we used the average ratio reported by (cite: He_2019) for Arp 240, CO ($2\rightarrow1$)/($1\rightarrow0$) = 0.85 $\pm$ 0.02.

what.value: Integrated measurements of normal spirals and starbursts for mK-S comparison

evidence.quote: We incorporate integrated measurements of both normal spirals and starbursts from (cite: Kennicutt2021)(brown and yellow squares).

what.value: 1.5-kpc-sized regions from a sample of 80 normal spiral galaxies from PHANGS

evidence.quote: Additionally, we include 1.5-kpc-sized regions from a sample of 80 normal spiral galaxies from PHANGS (cite: Sun_2023), represented by gray dots.

recipe.goal: Combine and image VLA radio continuum and ALMA CO(2-1) datasets at matched 1'' resolution
recipe.method: Combine configurations/arrays using CASA concat (4:1 A:C weight for VLA, equal weight for ALMA 7m+12m) and image with CASA tclean to a common 1'' restoring beam and 0.1'' pixel size.
key_parameters: restoringbeam = 1'', cell = 0.1'', uvtaper = 0.75'' (VLA), robust = 0.5 (VLA), spectral resolution = 3 km s^-1 (ALMA)
ALMA automasking: rms factor = 3, sidelobethresh = 2.0, noisethresh = 4.25, minbeamfrac = 0.3, lownoisethresh = 1.5, negativethresh = 0.0

recipe.goal: Apply uniform hexagonal grid and select detected regions
recipe.method: Overlay a uniform grid of hexagon-shaped tiles (each equal to the synthesized beam area of 1.13 arcsec^2 ~ 0.26 kpc^2) as photometric apertures, applying SNR thresholds to select overlapping and single-tracer detections.
key_parameters: Radio continuum threshold: 3-sigma; CO(2->1) threshold: > 2-sigma across at least 9 consecutive channels
assumptions: Cosmology: H0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_vacuum = 0.72, Omega_matter = 0.28, z = 0.02250, D_L = 98 Mpc, 1'' ~ 500 pc

recipe.goal: Derive Star Formation Rate surface density (Sigma_SFR) from 3 GHz radio continuum
recipe.method: Calculate SFR from 3 GHz luminosity using the Murphy et al. (2012) prescription (Eq. 1) and divide by the beam area (0.26 kpc^2) to obtain Sigma_SFR.
assumptions: Electron temperature T_e = 10^4 K, non-thermal spectral index alpha_NT = -0.85, Kroupa IMF, continuous SF over 100 Myr

recipe.goal: Derive molecular gas surface density (Sigma_H2), SFE, and depletion time (t_d)
recipe.method: Extract CO(2-1) line profiles per hexagon, sum over channels multiplied by 3 km s^-1 channel width, convert to L'_CO(1-0), multiply by alpha_CO to get M_H2, divide by beam area in pc^2 for Sigma_H2, and compute SFE = Sigma_SFR / Sigma_H2 and t_d = 1 / SFE.

recipe.goal: Measure molecular gas linewidth, turbulent pressure (P_turb), free-fall time (t_ff), and SFE per free-fall time (epsilon_ff)
recipe.method: Fit single or multiple Gaussian profiles to CO(2-1) spectra in each hexagon using scipy.optimize.leastsq to obtain average sigma linewidth <sigma>, then compute P_turb/k_B (Eq. 6), t_ff (Eq. 8), and epsilon_ff (Eq. 9).
assumptions: Linewidth is turbulently broadened; beam filling factor = 1; constant scale height H = 100 pc

recipe.goal: Evaluate distributions and fit the mK-S law slope globally and by morphological component
recipe.method: Compute skewness and fit 1- and 2-component Gaussian Mixture Models (evaluated with AIC and BIC) to Log Sigma_H2 and Log Sigma_SFR distributions; fit power-law slope N of Log(Sigma_SFR) vs Log(Sigma_H2) using ODR, Linmix (with and without upper limits), and ASURV survival analysis.
key_parameters: GMM components = 1 and 2; Linmix MCMC iterations = 10^4

recipe.goal: Quantify correlations between star formation and kinematic properties and map intensity gradients
recipe.method: Compute non-parametric Spearman's rank correlation coefficients (rho and p-value) at 16th, 50th, and 84th percentiles between Sigma_H2, Sigma_SFR, SFE and <sigma>, P_turb; compute normalized intensity gradient vectors for CO(2-1) and radio continuum.
key_parameters: Statistical significance threshold: rho > 0.30 and p-value < 0.03 (weak: 0.30-0.40, moderate: 0.40-0.60, strong: > 0.60)

score_reason: The ALMA project code, CASA version, array combination weights, automasking parameters, physical equations, conversion factors, detection thresholds, and regression tools (ODR, Linmix, ASURV, scikit-learn, SciPy) are all clearly documented. Minor deductions for delegating VLA observation details to earlier papers and omitting exact hexagonal grid anchoring coordinates and a few ALMA-specific tclean settings.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA data (2015.1.00804.S) and published VLA data with a well-specified imaging, aperture photometry, and Bayesian regression recipe leading to concrete numerical answer keys (mK-S slopes N, median SFE, linewidths, and Spearman rank correlations).
